correctness.rationale: Classical weighted PAV yields a continuous finite piecewise-linear map with locally attainable block-averaging derivatives. A finite coarea identity gives the exact cut formula. Row-stochasticity bounds every binary cut output in the unit cube, whose sharp Gini diameter is floor(n^2/4). A dominant-mass block gives the matching limit; finite-mass strictness follows from separate singleton versus non-singleton cut bounds. Double stochasticity proves equal-mass contraction. For n=4, size-two cuts are never amplifying and singleton cuts reduce to a pooled block of size 1, 2, 3 or 4; only adjacent two-blocks can amplify, proving the ratio-three criterion. Standard-library exact rational checks across all branch partitions and cuts in selected dimensions confirm relevant formulas; they are not used to prove unrestricted quantifiers.

value.rationale: The claim quantifies a natural but consequential mismatch between observation-weighted least-squares optimality and unweighted all-pairs dispersion stability. It gives exact finite fixed-weight evaluation, a sharp growing dimension envelope (~n/4), strict nonattainment under positive finite masses, and a complete n=4 nonexpansivity criterion with explicit witnesses. These are not mere software reproduction or an arbitrary finite slice: the four-site result is the first dimension permitting amplification, and the global rate quantifies how bad mass imbalance can become.
